messages:
Maya S.: FYI escalated from CS — AcmeCorp users keep getting kicked to MFA repeatedly after they finish the flow. Happens across Chrome/Firefox, ~20% of sessions. They said it started after last week's auth deploy.

Chris W.: Do we have an example user id / session id? any HTTP traces?

Maya S.: Customer provided a trace: session_id=abc123; their webapp calls /auth/mfa/verify -> 200, then next request to /api/generate returns 401. They pasted the headers:

```
Request: GET /api/generate
Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; device_trust=1
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>

Response: 401 Unauthorized
Set-Cookie: session=deleted; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT
Set-Cookie: session="s:VRY..."; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=300
```

Maya S.: Notice the immediate deletion and re-set. Customer suspects cookies flipping.

support-bot: Logged ticket #SUP-4783 and attached headers and sample curl.

Sanjay P.: Two quick checks: 1) Is refresh token TTL shorter than session cookie TTL? 2) Any cookie size >4KB that might cause browser truncation?

Emily R.: I looked at deploy notes — we rolled out auth-server v2 last Wed which introduced aggressive cookie rotation: we now rotate session cookie on every MFA auth to propagate new device_trust flag. Might be related.

Chris W.: Possible race window: client calls verify -> server rotates cookie with new token, but client makes another API call using old cookie or an old bearer token. If server sees mismatch between cookie and token it nukes session. Do we log token ids?

Maya S.: Customer included timeline: verify at 12:03:11, subsequent API at 12:03:11.120 (120ms later) — so super tight.

Sanjay P.: That fits race. Also noticed Set-Cookie uses SameSite=Lax. If any cross-site post happens (iframe/redirect), browser may not send replaced cookie immediately. For Chrome that can cause short-lived inconsistent state.

Emily R.: Repro steps I tried locally:
1) enable device_trust rotation in flags
2) run curl script that fires verify then API request with tiny delay (0-200ms)
Result: ~30% API calls get 401 and new Set-Cookie. Here's the quick repro curl:

```
# verify
curl -i -X POST https://auth.example.com/auth/mfa/verify -c cookies.txt -d '{"code":"123456"}'
# immediate followup
curl -i -X GET https://api.example.com/api/generate -b cookies.txt
```

Maya S.: Customer wants a short-term workaround they can apply ASAP.

Chris W.: Short-term options: 1) on auth server, don't rotate cookie in-place on MFA — instead return a header hint and rotate asynchronously; 2) ensure Set-Cookie uses SameSite=None; 3) add 200-300ms debounce before client makes follow-up calls.

Sanjay P.: We should avoid telling customers to change client behavior if we can fix server. Quick fix: change cookie rotation to set a new cookie name (session_next) and only swap after a subsequent validated request. That avoids immediate invalidation.

Emily R.: Patch proposal: when MFA handshake succeeds, set cookie with Max-Age longer (match refresh-token TTL) and do not expire old cookie until new cookie is accepted on next request. Rolling deployable in <4 hours.

Maya S.: Customer agreed to try a temporary client-side debounce (300ms) if we can push server change in next 48h. Can we get eng-security signoff?

Chris W.: Looping in eng-security — @eng-security please weigh in re: refresh token/session TTL consistency and any security concerns with delaying rotation.

eng-security: Quick note — delaying immediate rotation slightly (while keeping refresh-token checks) is OK as long as the old cookie is still bound to the device via device_trust and we don't extend the refresh token validity. Need a short risk doc.

Maya S.: Action items:
- Emily to prepare a 2-step rollback-safe patch to avoid immediate expiry (ETA 4h).
- Chris to add additional logging for token id mismatch and surface metrics for 401-after-mfa.
- Sanjay to draft short risk doc for eng-security.
- Maya to share temporary client debounce suggestion with AcmeCorp.

support-bot: SUP-4783 updated: assigned to Emily R., priority=P1, due=+48h.

Maya S.: I'll update customer and keep thread here. Thanks all. :pray:
